description: This line plot illustrates the training loss evolution over iterations for six different model configurations, with the vertical axis representing “Loss” on a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, and the horizontal axis representing “#Iteration” on a linear scale from 0 to 140,000. The plot displays six distinct lines, each corresponding to a different model variant as indicated in the legend: “Vanilla” (purple, solid line), “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid line), “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid line), “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid line), “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid line), and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid line). All lines begin at a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a rapid initial decline, followed by a slower, more gradual decrease toward the end of the training period. At iteration 140,000, the “Vanilla” model has a loss of approximately 2.5, while “StrmLLM (n=64)” has a loss of approximately 2.62, “SepLLM (n=64)” has a loss of approximately 2.52, “SepLLM (n=64, H)” has a loss of approximately 2.52, “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” has a loss of approximately 2.51, and “SepLLM (n=128)” has a loss of approximately 2.51. The “Vanilla” model consistently achieves the lowest loss throughout training, while the “StrmLLM (n=64)” model maintains the highest loss across the entire training duration.
